subject: chemistry
subtopic_label: Redox processes: electron transfer and changes in oxidation number (oxidation state)
stem: Which compound contains two different elements with identical oxidation states?
stem_lead: Which compound contains two different elements with identical oxidation states?

options.A: HClO
options.B: Mg(OH)₂
options.C: Na₂SO₄
options.D: NH₄Cl

learn_by_solve.solve: HClO (HOCl): H is +1, O is −2, so Cl is +1. Hydrogen and chlorine are two different elements with the same oxidation state. Mg(OH)₂ is Mg +2, O −2, H +1 — three different states; two OH groups are the same elements repeated, not two different elements sharing a state. Na₂SO₄ is Na +1, S +6, O −2. NH₄Cl is N −3, H +1, Cl −1. Only HClO has a matching pair.

B.pathway: Student reads (OH)₂ as ‘two elements with the same oxidation state’: two hydroxide units are the same two elements repeated, and in OH oxygen is −2 while hydrogen is +1.

followup.stem: Mg(OH)₂ has two hydroxide groups. In each OH, what are the oxidation states of O and H?

options.A: Both −1, so two different elements share the same state
options.B: O is −2 and H is +1, so O and H do not share a state
options.C: Both +1, matching magnesium
options.D: O is −1 and H is −1 because OH is the hydroxide ion

followup.why: Hydroxide is O −2 and H +1. Repeating OH twice does not create two different elements with the same oxidation state. Magnesium is +2, which matches neither.

C.pathway: Student does not complete 2(+1) + S + 4(−2) = 0 for Na₂SO₄, so they never see Na +1, S +6, O −2 as three different states (or they use sulfite S +4).

followup.stem: In Na₂SO₄, Na is +1 and O is −2. What is the oxidation state of S?

options.B: +4 (as in sulfite)

followup.why: 2(+1) + S + 4(−2) = 0 gives S = +6. The three elements are +1, +6 and −2. No two different elements share a state. Two sodium atoms are the same element.

D.pathway: Student assigns Cl in NH₄Cl as +1 (as in HCl or HClO) so that H +1 and Cl +1 look like a matching pair. Chlorine here is chloride, Cl −1.

followup.stem: What is the oxidation state of chlorine in NH₄Cl?

options.A: +1, as in HClO
options.B: −1, as chloride
options.C: +5, as in chlorate
options.D: 0, as Cl₂

followup.why: NH₄Cl is ammonium chloride: Cl is −1. Nitrogen in NH₄⁺ is −3 and hydrogen is +1. None of N, H and Cl share an oxidation state. Cl +1 is the HClO assignment, not this salt.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 39

This was the most challenging question on the paper with only the strongest candidates correctly giving the
answer, A. The most commonly chosen incorrect answers were C and D. All three compounds have an –OH

ketone or a methyl alcohol group, so none of them will give a positive iodoform test. It is possible for Z to be
ethanoic acid, or pentan-3-ol, or propan-1-ol, making the correct answer A.

stem:
Ethane-1,2-diol has the following structure.

Displayed structure: HOCH₂CH₂OH.

Without breaking the C–C bond, there are five possible oxidation products.

What is the total number of aldehyde groups and carboxylic acid groups in these five products?
stem_lead:
Ethane-1,2-diol has the following structure.

Displayed structure: HOCH₂CH₂OH.

Without breaking the C–C bond, there are five possible oxidation products.

What is the total number of aldehyde groups and carboxylic acid groups in these five products?

options.A: –CHO: 3; –COOH: 3
options.B: –CHO: 3; –COOH: 4
options.C: –CHO: 4; –COOH: 3
options.D: –CHO: 4; –COOH: 4

examiner_comment.text:
Question 27

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was A. The five possible products are HO2CCO2H, HO2CCHO,
HO2CCH2OH, OHCCHO, OHCCH2OH. The answer is therefore four –CO2H groups and four –CHO groups.
Candidates who chose A may not have realised that HO2CCH2OH and OHCCH2OH are also oxidation
products of CH2OHCH2OH.

learn_by_solve.solve: What is the total number of aldehyde groups and carboxylic acid groups in these five products? Required: D — –CHO: 4; –COOH: 4. A would need “–COOH: 3”, but the item needs “–COOH: 4”. B would need “–CHO: 3”, but the item needs “–CHO: 4”. C would need “–COOH: 3”, but the item needs “–COOH: 4”.

A.pathway: dropping a stated condition so “–COOH: 3” looked possible instead of “–COOH: 4”

followup.stem: Option A. –CHO: 3; –COOH: 3 has hydroxide groups. In each OH, what are the oxidation states of O and H?

options.A: Both −1, so two different elements share the same state
options.B: O is −2 and H is +1, so O and H do not share a state
options.C: Both +1, matching the metal
options.D: O is −1 and H is −1 because OH is the hydroxide ion

followup.why: Hydroxide is O −2 and H +1. Repeating OH does not give two different elements the same state. (O -2, H +1, C +3)

followup.stem: Option B. Is “–CHO: 3; –COOH: 4” the total number of aldehyde groups and carboxylic acid groups in these five products?

options.C: “–CHO: 3; –COOH: 4” would be correct if one stated condition were dropped
options.D: “–CHO: 3; –COOH: 4” and every other option are equally valid

followup.why: Option B used “–CHO: 3”; the item needs “–CHO: 4”.

C.pathway: dropping a stated condition so “–COOH: 3” looked possible instead of “–COOH: 4”

followup.stem: Option C. –CHO: 4; –COOH: 3 has hydroxide groups. In each OH, what are the oxidation states of O and H?

options.A: Both −1, so two different elements share the same state
options.B: O is −2 and H is +1, so O and H do not share a state

options.D: O is −1 and H is −1 because OH is the hydroxide ion

options.D: 1 only is correct

examiner_comment.text:
Question 40

The most commonly chosen incorrect answers were C and D. Candidates answered well by drawing
structures. Structure 1 is produced when one ester link forms between two lactic acid molecules, which lose
one water molecule. Structure 2 is produced when two ester links form between two lactic acid molecules,
which lose two water molecules. Careful examination of Structure 3 shows it has only five carbon atoms.
Carbon atoms are not lost in esterification, so Structure 3 cannot be an ester formed by two lactic acid
molecules.
Cambridge International Advanced Subsidiary and Advanced Level
9701 Chemistry March 2018
Principal Examiner Report for Teachers

31 per cent of candidates chose the correct answer, A. The most commonly chosen incorrect option was D.
This suggests that these candidates were able to conclude correctly that O and Cl
+ have the same number
of unpaired electrons in p orbitals, so statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is also true, F+ and Ga– both have two
unpaired p electrons. Statement 3 is also true, N and Kr3+ both have three unpaired p electrons. Therefore,
all three statements are true, and the correct answer is A.

Cambridge International Advanced Subsidiary and Advanced Level
9701 Chemistry March 2019
Principal Examiner Report for Teachers

stem:
In this question you can assume that ¹H and ³H have the same chemical properties.

A sample of ethanal contains only one isotope of hydrogen, ¹H.

It is reduced to compound Z, C₂H₆O, in a nucleophilic addition reaction using NaBH₄. All the hydrogen atoms in the NaBH₄ are the ³H isotope.

CH₃CHO —NaBH₄→ C₂H₆O, compound Z

Compound Z is then oxidised back to ethanal and water.

C₂H₆O + [O] → CH₃CHO + H₂O

Which statement about the final mixture of products is correct?
stem_lead:

It is reduced to compound Z, C₂H₆O, in a nucleophilic addition reaction using NaBH₄. All the hydrogen atoms in the NaBH₄ are the ³H isotope.

CH₃CHO —NaBH₄→ C₂H₆O, compound Z

Compound Z is then oxidised back to ethanal and water.

C₂H₆O + [O] → CH₃CHO + H₂O

Which statement about the final mixture of products is correct?

options.A: Both ethanal and water contain ³H atoms.
options.B: Ethanal is the only product containing ³H atoms.
options.C: Neither ethanal nor water contain ³H atoms.
options.D: Water is the only product containing ³H atoms.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 27

Each option was chosen with approximate equal frequency, which suggests candidates were guessing. A
small number of candidates did not submit an answer. When ethanal is reduced by NaBH4 the product is
ethanol, CH3CH2OH. The –CH2OH group will contain one 1H atom and two 3H atoms. When this group is
oxidised back to –CHO a water molecule is produced, as described in the equation. This water molecule
must contain at least one of the two 3H atoms from the –CH2OH group. The ethanal molecule produced may
have the 1H atom from the –CH2OH group, or it may have one of the two 3H atoms from the
–CH2OH group. Therefore, both water and ethanal contain 3H atoms.

Candidates found this question challenging but would have found it easier if the displayed formula of the
ethanol product was drawn out, labelling the three hydrogen atoms in the –CH2OH group as 1H or 3H.

subject: chemistry
stem:
When reactant X is treated with a suitable reagent, products Y and Z are formed. Infrared spectra of X, Y and Z are shown.

Which row could be correct?
stem_lead:
When reactant X is treated with a suitable reagent, products Y and Z are formed. Infrared spectra of X, Y and Z are shown.

Which row could be correct?

options.A: X: 2,3-dimethylpent-2-ene; Y: propanone; Z: butanone
options.B: X: 2-methylpent-2-ene; Y: propanone; Z: propanoic acid
options.C: X: pent-2-ene; Y: ethanoic acid; Z: propanoic acid
options.D: X: propyl propanoate; Y: propan-1-ol; Z: propanoic acid

learn_by_solve.solve: Spectra: X is an alkene (no C=O, no O–H), Y is a ketone (C=O, no O–H), Z is a carboxylic acid (C=O + carboxyl canyon). Oxidative cleavage of 2-methylpent-2-ene gives propanone + propanoic acid. That is row B.

A.pathway: Student keeps two ketones and omits that one product spectrum is a carboxylic acid (canyon).

followup.stem: If product Z shows a very broad 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ O–H plus C=O, what functional group is Z?

options.A: Ketone
options.B: Alcohol
options.C: Carboxylic acid
options.D: Alkene

followup.why: Two ketones cannot explain an acid spectrum for Z.

C.pathway: Student assigns both cleavage fragments as acids, ignoring that a 2,2-disubstituted alkene carbon becomes a ketone.

followup.stem: Oxidative cleavage: a carbon of C=C that bears two alkyl groups and no H becomes which product class?

options.A: Carboxylic acid
options.B: Ketone
options.C: Primary alcohol
options.D: Aldehyde that cannot oxidise further

followup.why: Pent-2-ene would not give two acids matching Y (ketone) and Z (acid).

D.pathway: Student conflates ester hydrolysis with alkene cleavage.

followup.stem: Hydrolysis of propyl propanoate yields which pair?

options.A: Two ketones
options.B: An alkene and a ketone
options.C: Propan-1-ol and propanoic acid
options.D: Two alkenes

followup.why: X would then be an ester (C=O + C–O), not an alkene. The X spectrum is the alkene.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 38

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was D.
The structural formula for 2-hydroxybutanenitrile is CH3CH2CH(OH)CN. It can be deduced from the question
that this was formed by a nucleophilic addition reaction between HCN and CH3CH2CHO, which is propanal.
Since propanal forms when compound Y is heated with a mild oxidising agent, compound Y is propan-1-ol
and the correct answer is C.

On reaction with Br₂, Y gives a product, C₇H₁₂Br₂, which exists as a mixture of four optical isomers.

options.A: 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane; SMILES: CC1(Br)CCCCC1
options.B: bromomethylcyclohexane; SMILES: BrCC1CCCCC1

examiner_comment.text:
Question 27

This was found to be a difficult question. The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C. Compound B
produces only one alkene when treated with hot alcoholic NaOH so it cannot be the answer. Compounds C
and D both produce two alkenes when treated with hot alcoholic NaOH. However, none of the alkenes
produced react with Br2 to form a non-chiral product. Compound A reacts with hot alcoholic NaOH to give
two products. If the C=C bond forms in the side chain, the product reacts with Br2 to form a non-chiral
product. If the C=C bond forms in the ring, the product reacts with Br2 to form a mixture of four optical
isomers. Therefore, compound A matches the description in the question.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 37

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C. 380 cm
3 of hydrogen is 380 ÷ 22400 moles at s.t.p.
This works out to be 0.01696 moles. Since two carboxylic acid molecules react with magnesium to give one
H2 molecule, there were 0.03393 moles of Q in 4.00 g, giving a relative formula mass of 118. Candidates
who incorrectly used the molar volume at room conditions, 24.0 dm3, will have calculated 0.01583 moles of
hydrogen, therefore 0.03167 moles of Q. This then gives a relative formula mass of 126, explaining the
choice of answer C.

subject: chemistry
stem:
The infrared spectrum of an organic compound is shown.

Which compound could give this spectrum?
stem_lead:
The infrared spectrum of an organic compound is shown.

Which compound could give this spectrum?

options.A: CH₃CH₂CO₂H
options.B: CH₃CH(OH)CH₃
options.C: CH₃COCH₃
options.D: CH₃COCH₂OH

headers: characteristic infrared absorption range (in wavenumbers) / cm⁻¹

learn_by_solve.solve: The spectrum has a deep sharp C=O near 1700–1750 cm⁻¹, no broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹, and no carboxyl canyon at 2500–3000 cm⁻¹. That is a ketone (propanone), not an acid, alcohol, or hydroxyketone.

A.pathway: Student treats any C=O as a carboxylic acid and omits the very broad 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ O–H canyon.

followup.stem: Which extra feature, besides a C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹, is required before you can call the compound a carboxylic acid?

options.A: A sharp peak at 2200–2250 cm⁻¹
options.B: A very broad O–H absorption spanning about 2500–3000 cm⁻¹
options.C: A sharp peak at 3300–3500 cm⁻¹
options.D: No absorption above 1500 cm⁻¹

followup.why: Carboxyl O–H is a canyon from about 2500–3000 cm⁻¹. A ketone has C=O without that canyon.

B.pathway: Student reads a C=O or fingerprint and names an alcohol, dropping the required broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹.

followup.stem: A liquid alcohol IR must show a broad O–H stretch. In which range does that band appear?

options.C: 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ (carboxyl canyon)

followup.why: Alcohol O–H is 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ and broad. 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ is the carboxylic acid canyon.

D.pathway: Student sees C=O and also names a hydroxyketone/hydroxyaldehyde, omitting that an alcohol O–H would still have to be present.

followup.stem: A molecule with both a ketone C=O and an alcohol O–H must show which pair of bands?

options.A: Sharp C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹ only
options.B: Broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ only
options.C: Both a sharp C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹ and a broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹
options.D: A nitrile band at 2200–2250 cm⁻¹

followup.why: Both groups are independent absorbers. Missing the alcohol O–H rules out a hydroxyketone.

Which functional group could the compound contain?

learn_by_solve.solve: Strong C=O near 1740 cm⁻¹ plus strong C–O near 1240 cm⁻¹, and no O–H above 3100 cm⁻¹: ester, not alcohol, acid, or nitrile.

options.B: A very broad O–H absorption spanning about 2500–3000 cm⁻¹

options.D: No absorption above 1500 cm⁻¹

followup.why: Carboxyl O–H is a canyon from about 2500–3000 cm⁻¹. A ketone has C=O without that canyon.

followup.why: If that 2200–2250 cm⁻¹ band is absent, the compound is not a nitrile.

Question 39

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was A. The structural formula of but-2-ene is CH3CHCHCH3.
Each hydrogen atom has one occupied s orbital only. The hydrogen atoms therefore do not need to be
considered. The two middle carbon atoms are sp2 hybridised, so they have no sp3 hybrid orbitals. The end
carbons are sp3 hybridised, they each have four sp3 hybrid orbitals. There are therefore eight sp3 hybridised
orbitals used in the bonding of but-2-ene.

Question 9

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was B. 180 cm3 of oxygen contains 7.5  10–3 moles. The

examiner_comment.text:
Question 38  the reaction of ethane with aqueous bromine in the presence of sodium bromide tests the
understanding of the mechanism of electrophilic addition.  An analysis of the answers yields the rather
surprising fact that 52% of candidates thought that it is possible to obtain CH 2ClCH2Cl, presumably by the
generation of C l2 and its subsequent addition to CH 2=CH2, and 24% believed it was not possible to get
CH2BrCH2Br.
One question had a low facility: in Question 21  candidates were asked the total number of different
chloroethanes that are possible with the formula C 2H6-nCln.  Only 19% gave the correct answer C, 9: by far
the greater proportion, 59%, opted for A, 6, not allowing for the structural isomers when n is 2, 3 and 4.
Two other questions require comment.  In Question 8 a significant proportion of candidates, 33%, opted for
the distractor C not appreciating that a ‘standard enthalpy change of combustion’ is estimated or measured
at a standard temperature – in this case, not the high temperature of combustion of carbon.  In Question 36
24% of candidates thought that strontium does not burn on being heated in oxygen.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 28 involved two processes: first the breakdown by hot concentrated acidified KMnO4 of carvone, a
cyclic unsaturated ketone, followed by the reaction of the product with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone reag ent.
There was an almost equal uptake of options A, B and C, so that the key C did not show good discrimination
among the ability range of candidates.  It is clear that many candidates did not correctly deduce the nature of
the breakdown of carvone under these oxidative conditions.
Although it performed satisfactorily, Question 19 deserves comment.  Candidates were asked to give t he
number of chiral centres in the ster oid testosterone: its skeletal form ula was given.  There was an almost
equal choice between the answers 2, 3 and 6  the c orrect answer being 6.  It would appear that most
candidates focused on the positions where there are substituent groups on the ring system, which indeed
are chiral centres, but omitted those carbon atoms within the ring system that possess chirality.

What can X be?

options.B: 1 and 2 only are correct
options.C: 2 and 3 only are correct
options.D: 1 only is correct

examiner_comment.text:
Question 35
Only 19% of candidates chose the correct answer, C.   The most popular answers were A and B, each
chosen by 34% of candidates.  It is clear from the number choosing A that for many candidates the key point
was whether or not statement 1 was tr ue, i.e., does the oxidation of CO “occur in the atmosphere”?  While
CO can be oxidised to CO
2 in fires or lightning strikes, this is a com bustion reaction, it is not “a reaction that
occurs in the atmosphere”, unlike the oxidation of NO to NO2, and the oxidation of SO2 to SO3, both of which
do occur “in the atmosphere”.  It is clear from the num ber choosing B that for many candidates the key point
was whether or not statement 3 was true .  Presumably they realised that SO 2 is an atmospheric pollutant
oxide, but they did not appreciate that the oxidation of SO2 to SO3 occurs “in the atmosphere”.
4

significant number may have guessed their response.  A few candidates either gave no answer or gave an
invalid answer to this question.  In Syllabus Section 9.4(f)(i)  candidates are required to “describe and explain
the reactions of halide ions with aqueous silver ions followed by aqueous ammonia”.  When silver chloride
dissolves in aqueous ammonia, (Ag(NH
3)2)+ is formed.  A co-ordinate bond is formed from ammonia to silver
ions, and the oxidation state of nitrogen remains -3.  Ammonia molecules do not receive protons in this
reaction, so ammonia does not act as a Brønsted-Lowry base, so only choices 1 and 2 are correct.
4

Question 26

that chose C did not appreciate that pentan-1-ol is oxid ised to propanoic acid which has stronger hydrogen

Question 37

24% of candidates chose the correct answer, B. The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C,

labelled carbon atom is also bonded to a hydrogen atom , therefore the bond angles around it are less than
120
o and the four labelled carbon atoms are not co-planar.

Question 39

involve H
+/Cr2O7
2- with immediate distillation, to give ethanal. Statement 3 describes the conditions as

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was B. For many candidates this question rested on whether

Question 38

The three incorrect choices each attracted approximately equal numbers of candidates, suggesting many
candidates may have guessed. Statement 1 is true because a primary halogenoalkane reacts mainly by an
S

The diagram shows the monomer used to make polyvinyl chloride, PVC. Assuming that one particular molecule of the polymer forms from n molecules of the monomer (where n is many thousands), which statements are correct?

1  The relative molecular mass of this polymer molecule is approximately 62.5n.
2  There are n chiral carbon atoms in this polymer molecule.
3  There are 5n σ bonds in one polymer molecule.

options.A: 1, 2 and 3 are correct
options.B: 1 and 2 only are correct
options.C: 2 and 3 only are correct
options.D: 1 only is correct

statements.text: The relative molecular mass of this polymer molecule is approximately 62.5n.
There are n chiral carbon atoms in this polymer molecule.
There are 5n σ bonds in one polymer molecule.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 38

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was D. Since each of the carbon atoms bonded to a chlorine
atom will be chiral, if there are n monomer residues then the number of chiral carbon atoms is also n. There
are, therefore, n chiral carbon atoms in each molecule. Statement 2 is therefore correct and the answer is B.

9701 Chemistry June 2017

examiner_comment.text:
Question 21

The most commonly chosen incorrect answers were A and B. The structure should start with a cyclopentyl
ring with an OH group and a methyl group on carbon atom 1. There is one carbon atom left to add.

Cambridge International Advanced Subsidiary and Advanced Level
9701 Chemistry June 2017
Principal Examiner Report for Teachers

  © 2017
• If this carbon atom goes on carbon atom 2 of the ring as a methyl group we have a molecule with two
chiral centres and therefore four isomers.
• If this carbon atom goes on carbon atom 3 of the ring as a methyl group we have a molecule with two
chiral centres and therefore four more isomers, making eight so far.
• If this carbon atom goes on the methyl group already  attached to carbon atom 1 this becomes an ethyl
group. This molecule is not chiral, giving one more isomer, making nine.

The student’s results are recorded in the table.

2  The concentration of the hydrogen peroxide solution used was 4.0 mol dm⁻³.
3  The MnO₂ used in experiment 1 was in larger pieces than the MnO₂ used in experiment 2.

greater time not a smaller time.

stem:
Compound X contains three carbon atoms. Part of a simplified infra-red spectrum of compound X is shown.

Which compound could be X?
stem_lead:
Compound X contains three carbon atoms. Part of a simplified infra-red spectrum of compound X is shown.

Which compound could be X?

options.A: CH₃CH₂CHO
options.B: CH₃CH₂CO₂H
options.C: CH₃CH₂CH₂OH
options.D: CH₃CO₂CH₃

learn_by_solve.solve: Three carbons, broad alcohol O–H (3200–3600 cm⁻¹), C–O near 1000–1050 cm⁻¹, CH₂ scissor near 1465 cm⁻¹, and no C=O. That is propan-1-ol, not the aldehyde, acid or ester.

A.pathway: Student expects an aldehyde from a simplified fingerprint and omits the aldehyde C=O (~1730) plus C–H ~2700–2800 cm⁻¹.

followup.stem: Propanal would show a strong C=O. Roughly where?
followup.why: No C=O on this spectrum rules out the aldehyde.

B.pathway: Student treats any C=O as a carboxylic acid and omits the very broad 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ O–H canyon.

followup.stem: Which extra feature, besides a C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹, is required before you can call the compound a carboxylic acid?

options.A: A sharp peak at 2200–2250 cm⁻¹
options.B: A very broad O–H absorption spanning about 2500–3000 cm⁻¹
options.C: A sharp peak at 3300–3500 cm⁻¹
options.D: No absorption above 1500 cm⁻¹

followup.why: Carboxyl O–H is a canyon from about 2500–3000 cm⁻¹. A ketone has C=O without that canyon.

D.pathway: Student conflates ester C–O with alcohol C–O, ignoring that an ester also has a strong C=O near 1740 cm⁻¹.

followup.stem: An ester such as methyl ethanoate must show which pair?

options.A: O–H 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ only
options.B: C=O near 1740 cm⁻¹ and C–O near 1050–1250 cm⁻¹
options.C: C≡N at 2200 cm⁻¹
options.D: Carboxyl canyon 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ only

followup.why: No C=O rules out the ester. Alcohol C–O is not enough.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 9

hydroxylammonium ions is –1. If two Fe

The infra-red spectrum of an organic compound is shown.

Which compound could give this spectrum?

Which compound could give this spectrum?

options.B: CH₃CH(OH)CH₃
options.C: CH₃COCH₃
options.D: CH₃COCH₂OH

examiner_comment.text:
Question 30

The most commonly chosen incorrect answers were A and D. The lack of a broad absorption between 2500
and 3000 cm
–1 rules out A. The lack of a broad absorption between 3200 and 3600 cm–1 rules out B and D.

learn_by_solve.solve: The spectrum has a deep sharp C=O near 1700–1750 cm⁻¹, no broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹, and no carboxyl canyon at 2500–3000 cm⁻¹. That is a ketone (propanone), not an acid, alcohol, or hydroxyketone.

A.pathway: Student treats any C=O as a carboxylic acid and omits the very broad 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ O–H canyon.

followup.stem: Which extra feature, besides a C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹, is required before you can call the compound a carboxylic acid?

options.A: A sharp peak at 2200–2250 cm⁻¹
options.B: A very broad O–H absorption spanning about 2500–3000 cm⁻¹
options.C: A sharp peak at 3300–3500 cm⁻¹
options.D: No absorption above 1500 cm⁻¹

followup.why: Carboxyl O–H is a canyon from about 2500–3000 cm⁻¹. A ketone has C=O without that canyon.

B.pathway: Student reads a C=O or fingerprint and names an alcohol, dropping the required broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹.

followup.stem: A liquid alcohol IR must show a broad O–H stretch. In which range does that band appear?

options.C: 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ (carboxyl canyon)

followup.why: Alcohol O–H is 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ and broad. 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ is the carboxylic acid canyon.

D.pathway: Student sees C=O and also names a hydroxyketone/hydroxyaldehyde, omitting that an alcohol O–H would still have to be present.

followup.stem: A molecule with both a ketone C=O and an alcohol O–H must show which pair of bands?

options.A: Sharp C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹ only
options.B: Broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ only
options.C: Both a sharp C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹ and a broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹
options.D: A nitrile band at 2200–2250 cm⁻¹

followup.why: Both groups are independent absorbers. Missing the alcohol O–H rules out a hydroxyketone.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 38

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C. An alcohol that gives a positive iodoform test must
have a -CH(OH)CH
3 group.
• Ethanol does but ethane-1,2-diol doesn’t, so pair 1 can be distinguished.
• Propan-2-ol does but methylpropan-2-ol doesn’t, so pair 2 can be distinguished.
• Ethanol does and butan-2-ol does, so pair 3 cannot  be distinguished and the correct answer is B.

Cambridge International Advanced Subsidiary and Advanced Level
9701 Chemistry June 2018

stem:
The infra-red spectrum of a substance with empirical formula C₂H₄O is shown.

Which bonds are responsible for peak X and peak Y?
stem_lead:
The infra-red spectrum of a substance with empirical formula C₂H₄O is shown.

Which bonds are responsible for peak X and peak Y?

options.A: peak X: C–H; peak Y: C=C
options.B: peak X: C–H; peak Y: C=O
options.C: peak X: O–H; peak Y: C=C
options.D: peak X: O–H; peak Y: C=O

learn_by_solve.solve: Empirical formula C₂H₄O. Peak X is in the C–H stretch region (~2900); peak Y is the C=O (~1700). That is ethanal (or similar). Not O–H (no broad high-ν band) and not C=C as the strong Y.

A.pathway: Student substitutes C=C for C=O at ~1700 cm⁻¹.

followup.stem: A strong sharp band near 1700 cm⁻¹ is which bond in this table?

options.A: C=C (1500–1680 cm⁻¹, usually weaker)

followup.why: Y is the carbonyl, not C=C.

C.pathway: Student labels a C–H stretch as O–H.

followup.stem: O–H (alcohol) is broad and sits at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹. A sharper band near 2900 cm⁻¹ is usually which bond?

options.A: O–H
options.B: C=O
options.C: C–H
options.D: C≡N

followup.why: X is C–H, not O–H. There is no broad alcohol band.

D.pathway: Student assigns O–H and C=O as if the molecule were a carboxylic acid, omitting that X is not a canyon.

followup.stem: Carboxyl O–H is a very broad canyon at 2500–3000 cm⁻¹. If peak X is a relatively sharp band near 2900 cm⁻¹, is it carboxyl O–H?

options.A: Yes, all bands near 2900 cm⁻¹ are O–H
options.B: No — that shape and position are C–H
options.C: Yes, if a C=O is also present
options.D: No — carboxyl O–H is at 2200 cm⁻¹

followup.why: C₂H₄O with C–H + C=O is the aldehyde, not the acid.

stem:
Ethanedioic acid, HO₂CCO₂H, can be oxidised by KMnO₄ in dilute sulfuric acid. The products of this reaction are carbon dioxide, water, potassium sulfate and manganese(II) sulfate.

In this reaction each ethanedioic acid molecule loses two electrons as it is oxidised. A half-equation for this process is shown.

HO₂CCO₂H → 2CO₂ + 2H⁺ + 2e⁻

How many water molecules are produced when five ethanedioic acid molecules are oxidised by KMnO₄ in dilute sulfuric acid?
stem_lead:

In this reaction each ethanedioic acid molecule loses two electrons as it is oxidised. A half-equation for this process is shown.

HO₂CCO₂H → 2CO₂ + 2H⁺ + 2e⁻

How many water molecules are produced when five ethanedioic acid molecules are oxidised by KMnO₄ in dilute sulfuric acid?

examiner_comment.text:
Question 9

The most commonly chosen incorrect option was C. From the information in the question, each ethanedioic
acid molecule loses two electrons when it is oxidised and each manganese atom gains five electrons when it
is reduced. Therefore, five ethanedioic acid molecules are oxidised by two manganate(VII) ions. This means
that one formula unit of potassium sulfate and two formula units of manganese(II) are produced. This
requires three formula units of sulfuric acid in the reactants. Three formula units of sulfuric acid plus five
molecules of ethanedioic acid contain a total of 16 hydrogen atoms, so eight water molecules are formed.
Therefore, B is the correct answer.

subject: chemistry
stem:
The diagram shows the infra-red spectrum of Q.

What could be Q?
stem_lead:
The diagram shows the infra-red spectrum of Q.

What could be Q?

options.A: butan-1-ol
options.B: butanoic acid
options.C: butanone
options.D: 3-hydroxybutanal

learn_by_solve.solve: Q shows C=O and no O–H: butanone. Butan-1-ol has alcohol O–H; butanoic acid has the canyon; 3-hydroxybutanal has both C=O and O–H.

A.pathway: Student reads a C=O or fingerprint and names an alcohol, dropping the required broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹.

followup.stem: A liquid alcohol IR must show a broad O–H stretch. In which range does that band appear?

options.C: 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ (carboxyl canyon)

followup.why: Alcohol O–H is 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ and broad. 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ is the carboxylic acid canyon.

B.pathway: Student treats any C=O as a carboxylic acid and omits the very broad 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ O–H canyon.

followup.stem: Which extra feature, besides a C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹, is required before you can call the compound a carboxylic acid?

options.A: A sharp peak at 2200–2250 cm⁻¹
options.B: A very broad O–H absorption spanning about 2500–3000 cm⁻¹
options.C: A sharp peak at 3300–3500 cm⁻¹
options.D: No absorption above 1500 cm⁻¹

followup.why: Carboxyl O–H is a canyon from about 2500–3000 cm⁻¹. A ketone has C=O without that canyon.

D.pathway: Student sees C=O and also names a hydroxyketone/hydroxyaldehyde, omitting that an alcohol O–H would still have to be present.

followup.stem: A molecule with both a ketone C=O and an alcohol O–H must show which pair of bands?

options.A: Sharp C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹ only
options.B: Broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ only
options.C: Both a sharp C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹ and a broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹
options.D: A nitrile band at 2200–2250 cm⁻¹

followup.why: Both groups are independent absorbers. Missing the alcohol O–H rules out a hydroxyketone.

stem:
The volume of carbon dioxide collected by reacting 0.100 mol of magnesium carbonate with 50.0 cm³ of 1.00 mol dm⁻³ sulfuric acid is measured against time. The volume produced is plotted against time and the line labelled P on the graph is obtained.

The graph has the y-axis labelled volume of CO₂ / cm³ and the x-axis labelled time / s. Line P rises steeply from the origin and levels off at a lower volume. Line Q rises from the origin with an approximately straight initial section and levels off at a higher volume.

The experiment is repeated using 0.100 mol of the same magnesium carbonate, and a different sample of acid. All other conditions remain the same. Plotting these results gives the line labelled Q.

Which sample of acid could give the line labelled Q?

Question 39

The most commonly chosen incorrect option was C. For most candidates this question depended on the

What could X be?

2  methyl butanoate
3  1-hydroxypentan-3-one

1  ethyl propanoate
2  methyl butanoate
3  1-hydroxypentan-3-one

learn_by_solve.solve: C₅H₁₀O₂, strong 1250 cm⁻¹ (C–O), strong 1720 cm⁻¹ (C=O), no strong peak above 3100 cm⁻¹ (no O–H). Ethyl propanoate and methyl butanoate are esters that fit. 1-hydroxypentan-3-one has an alcohol O–H above 3100 cm⁻¹, so 3 is out. Key B (1 and 2 only).

followup.stem: A strong peak above 3100 cm⁻¹ in this context is which group?

options.A: Ester C=O
options.B: Alcohol O–H
options.C: C–H of CH₃ only
options.D: C–O of an ester

followup.why: Statement 3 has an alcohol, which would absorb above 3100 cm⁻¹. It is out.

options.B: Yes
options.C: No, esters have no C=O
options.D: Only methyl esters do

followup.why: Both isomeric esters fit. Do not drop statement 1.

followup.stem: Methyl butanoate and ethyl propanoate are isomers. Do they share the same IR functional-group pattern?

options.A: No — only ethyl esters show C=O
options.B: No — only methyl esters show C–O
options.C: Yes — both are esters: C=O + C–O, no O–H
options.D: Yes — both are alcohols

followup.why: Both 1 and 2 are correct.

The table shows the molecular formulae of three molecules P, Q and R. None of the molecules are cyclic.

molecule | molecular formula
P | CH₄O
Q | CH₂O₂
R | CH₂O

Which molecules show a strong absorption between 1610 cm⁻¹ and 1750 cm⁻¹ in their infra-red spectra?
stem_lead:
The table shows the molecular formulae of three molecules P, Q and R. None of the molecules are cyclic.

molecule | molecular formula
P | CH₄O
Q | CH₂O₂
R | CH₂O

Which molecules show a strong absorption between 1610 cm⁻¹ and 1750 cm⁻¹ in their infra-red spectra?

options.A: Q only
options.B: R only
options.C: Q and R only
options.D: P, Q and R

learn_by_solve.solve: P is CH₄O = methanol (alcohol, no C=O). Q is CH₂O₂ = methanoic acid (C=O). R is CH₂O = methanal (C=O). Strong 1610–1750 cm⁻¹ is C=O, so Q and R only.

A.pathway: Student omits methanal’s C=O.

followup.stem: Methanal (CH₂O) is an aldehyde. Does it have a C=O absorption in 1610–1750 cm⁻¹?

options.A: No, aldehydes have no C=O
options.B: Yes
options.C: Only if an O–H is also present
options.D: Only in the fingerprint region

followup.why: R belongs with Q. The answer is Q and R.

B.pathway: Student omits the acid’s C=O.

followup.stem: Methanoic acid (CH₂O₂) contains which bond that absorbs at 1610–1750 cm⁻¹?

options.A: O–H only
options.B: C=O
options.C: C≡N
options.D: None — acids are silent there

followup.why: Q has C=O as well. Not R only.

D.pathway: Student over-extends C=O to methanol because it contains oxygen.

followup.stem: Methanol is CH₃OH. Does it have a C=O?

options.A: Yes, all oxygen compounds have C=O
options.B: Yes, at 3200 cm⁻¹
options.C: No — it has C–O and O–H, not C=O
options.D: No — methanol is an alkane

followup.why: P does not absorb as a carbonyl. Not all three.

stem:
The diagram shows the infrared spectrum of an organic compound.

What could be the identity of this compound?
stem_lead:
The diagram shows the infrared spectrum of an organic compound.

options.B: propanal
options.C: propanoic acid
options.D: propanone

learn_by_solve.solve: Very broad O–H from ~2500–3300 cm⁻¹ plus a sharp C=O near 1710 cm⁻¹ is the carboxyl signature. That is the acid, not the alcohol (O–H higher and no C=O), aldehyde/ketone (C=O, no canyon), or ester (C=O + C–O, no O–H).

A.pathway: Student swaps carboxyl O–H for alcohol O–H.

followup.stem: Alcohol O–H and carboxyl O–H sit in different ranges. Which pairing is correct?

options.A: Alcohol 2500–3000 cm⁻¹; carboxyl 3200–3600 cm⁻¹
options.B: Alcohol 3200–3600 cm⁻¹; carboxyl 2500–3000 cm⁻¹
options.C: Both 1640–1750 cm⁻¹
options.D: Both 2200–2250 cm⁻¹

followup.why: A canyon centred near 3000 cm⁻¹ is carboxyl, not a simple alcohol.

B.pathway: Student names the aldehyde from C=O and omits that an aldehyde has no O–H canyon.

followup.stem: If the spectrum shows a very broad O–H spanning 2500–3000 cm⁻¹, can the compound be propanal?

options.A: Yes — aldehydes always show that canyon
options.B: Yes — that band is aldehyde C–H
options.C: No — propanal has C=O but not a carboxyl O–H canyon
options.D: No — aldehydes absorb only below 1000 cm⁻¹

followup.why: The canyon is carboxyl O–H. Propanal does not have it.

D.pathway: Student names the ketone from C=O and omits the O–H canyon sitting on top of it.

followup.stem: Propanone has a sharp C=O and no O–H. What would you not see for propanone?

options.A: A sharp band near 1715 cm⁻¹
options.B: Alkyl C–H near 2900 cm⁻¹
options.C: A very broad absorption from 2500–3300 cm⁻¹
options.D: Fingerprint peaks below 1500 cm⁻¹

followup.why: The broad 2500–3300 cm⁻¹ canyon rules out a simple ketone.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 20

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was B.
The product nitrile has the carbon atom of the nitrile group, not the nitrogen atom, joined to the C 2H5 group,
so the answer is A or B. The SN2 mechanism involves attack by a lone pair on a positively charged carbon
atom, and does not involve the formation of a carbocation, so the answer is A.

stem:
Compound X has the empirical formula C₂H₄O. Its infra-red spectrum is shown.

What could be the skeletal formula of compound X?
stem_lead:
Compound X has the empirical formula C₂H₄O. Its infra-red spectrum is shown.

What could be the skeletal formula of compound X?

options.A: CH₃C(=O)OCH₂CH₃
options.B: five-membered cyclic ester, oxolan-2-one
options.C: OHCCH=CHCH₂OH
options.D: CH₃C(=O)CH(OH)CH₃

learn_by_solve.solve: Empirical C₂H₄O, IR of an ester (C=O ~1740, C–O ~1240, no O–H): ethyl ethanoate. Cyclic ester would fit IR but the question asks the skeletal formula that matches this acyclic ester. C and D have O–H (and C has C=C).

B.pathway: Student over-extends ‘ester IR’ to a cyclic ester that is not the molecule implied by the plotted (ethyl ethanoate) pattern / formula pairing used here.

followup.stem: C₂H₄O for ethyl ethanoate is the empirical formula of C₄H₈O₂. A C₄ cyclic ester is an isomer. What extra check still favours ethyl ethanoate on a typical 9701 ester plot?

options.A: Cyclic esters have O–H
options.B: The acyclic acetate pattern (C=O + C–O, no O–H) plus the usual teaching example
options.C: Cyclic esters have C≡N
options.D: Empirical formula forbids C₄ esters

followup.why: The intended structure is ethyl ethanoate, not the lactone.

C.pathway: Student sees C=O and also names a hydroxyketone/hydroxyaldehyde, omitting that an alcohol O–H would still have to be present.

followup.stem: A molecule with both a ketone C=O and an alcohol O–H must show which pair of bands?

options.A: Sharp C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹ only
options.B: Broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ only
options.C: Both a sharp C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹ and a broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹
options.D: A nitrile band at 2200–2250 cm⁻¹

followup.why: Both groups are independent absorbers. Missing the alcohol O–H rules out a hydroxyketone.

subtopic_label: Chemical equilibria: reversible reactions, dynamic equilibrium
stem:
Ethanol combines with ethanoic acid to form ethyl ethanoate according to the following reaction.

9.2 g ethanol, 12 g ethanoic acid and 8.8 g ethyl ethanoate are mixed and allowed to stand at 298 K, until equilibrium is reached.
(Mᵣ: C₂H₅OH, 46; CH₃CO₂H, 60; CH₃CO₂C₂H₅, 88)

The resulting equilibrium mixture is found to contain 4.8 g ethanoic acid.

The experiment is repeated at 323 K.

Which statements are correct?

C₂H₅OH(l) + CH₃CO₂H(l) ⇌ CH₃CO₂C₂H₅(l) + H₂O(l)    ΔH⦵ = −6 kJ mol⁻¹

1  There are 0.22 moles of ethyl ethanoate in the mixture at equilibrium at 298 K.
2  The equilibrium mixture at 323 K will contain more than 4.8 g of ethanoic acid.
3  If a small amount of water is added at the start of either experiment the value of Kc would not be affected.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 31

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C.
To correctly answer this question, the following considerations were necessary:
• The original mixture is 0.2 mol ethanol, 0.2 mol ethanoic acid, 0.1 mol ethyl ethanoate.
• At equilibrium there is 0.08 mol ethanoic acid.
• At equilibrium there must also be 0.08 mol ethanol, 0.22 mol ethyl ethanoate and 0.12 mol water.

These deductions can then be made:
- Statement 1 is true.
- A higher temperature of 323 K favours the endothermic back reaction, so more reactants are
present at equilibrium, so statement 2 is true.
- K
c is not affected by the addition of water or any other substance, so statement 3 is  true.

stem:
The molecular formula of Z is C₄H₈O.

The infra-red spectrum of Z is shown.

What could be Z?
stem_lead:
The molecular formula of Z is C₄H₈O.

The infra-red spectrum of Z is shown.

What could be Z?

options.A: butan-2-one, CH₃CH₂COCH₃
options.B: cyclobutanol
options.C: butanoic acid, CH₃CH₂CH₂CO₂H
options.D: but-3-en-1-ol, CH₂=CHCH₂CH₂OH

examiner_comment.text:
Question 30

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C.
The answer cannot be C as butanoic acid does not fit the stated molecular formula. The O-H absorption
present on the left of the spectrum rules out A. The C=C absorption between 1600 and 1700 means that this
is the spectrum of D and not B.

learn_by_solve.solve: C₄H₈O. IR shows alcohol O–H and C=C (~1640), not C=O and not a carboxyl canyon. Butanoic acid is C₄H₈O₂ (wrong formula) and would show the canyon. Butanone has C=O, no O–H. Cyclobutanol has O–H but no C=C. But-3-en-1-ol fits.

A.pathway: Student matches a ketone to C₄H₈O and omits the O–H on the left of the plot.

followup.stem: The O–H absorption on the left of the spectrum rules out which class?

options.A: Alcohols
options.B: Carboxylic acids
options.C: Ketones such as butanone
options.D: Alkenes that also contain O–H

followup.why: Butanone has no O–H. Examiner: O–H rules out A.

B.pathway: Student keeps a cyclic alcohol and omits the C=C band at 1600–1700 cm⁻¹.

followup.stem: A band between 1600 and 1700 cm⁻¹ on this plot (with O–H, no C=O) is which bond?

options.A: C=O of a ketone
options.B: C=C of an alkene
options.C: C≡N
options.D: C–O of an ether only

followup.why: C=C means D, not cyclobutanol. Examiner comment matches this.

C.pathway: Student ignores the given molecular formula and names butanoic acid from an O–H shape.

followup.stem: Butanoic acid is C₄H₈O₂. Z is C₄H₈O. Can Z be butanoic acid?

options.A: Yes, IR overrides molecular formula
options.B: Yes, acids are always C₄H₈O
options.C: No — the formula does not match
options.D: No — acids have no O–H

followup.why: Examiner: C is the most common wrong answer; the formula already kills it.

options.D: 1 only is correct

examiner_comment.text:
Question 34

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was D.

2 is correct, as cooling the mixture will change the average kinetic energy of the gas particles. Adding a
catalyst will not affect the average kinetic energy of the gas particles, so the combined effect of these
changes is to lower the average kinetic energy of the gas particles.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 24

The most commonly chosen incorrect answers were B and C.
One possible correct approach to this question is:

35 cm
3 of CO2 and 55 cm3 of water is a 7:11 ratio.

A 1 molecule of C2H5OH and 3 molecules of CH3OH give 5CO2 and 9H2O. ratio 5:9.  Incorrect.
B 2 molecules of C2H5OH and 3 molecules of CH3OH give 7CO2 and 12H2O. ratio 7:12. Incorrect.
C 3 molecules of C2H5OH and 2 molecules of CH3OH give 8CO2 and 13H2O. ratio 8:13. Incorrect.
D 3 molecules of C2H5OH and 1 molecule of CH3OH give 7CO2 and 11H2O. ratio 7:11. Correct.

Question 39

The most common incorrect answer was B. Candidates found this very challenging and struggled to

stem:
‘Black powder’ is a mixture of potassium nitrate, carbon and sulfur. The mixture reacts as shown.

4KNO₃(s) + 7C(s) + S(s) → 3CO₂(g) + 3CO(g) + 2N₂(g) + K₂S(s) + K₂CO₃(s)

A sealed tube containing black powder has a volume of 10.0 cm³. When all of the black powder reacts, the reaction causes a pressure of 2 × 10⁶ Pa and a temperature of 2500 K.

The volume of the K₂CO₃ and K₂S produced can be ignored.

How many moles of KNO₃ are contained in the sealed tube?

examiner_comment.text:
Question 7

The most common incorrect answer was B. If the ideal gas equation, pV = nRT, is used

originally 0.5 × 9.63 × 10− 4 = 4.81 × 10− 4 moles of KNO3. It is possible that candidates who chose option B
used the ideal gas equation correctly but did not subsequently use the stoichiometry given in the equation.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 28

The most common incorrect answer was C. Compound C reacts with hot ethanolic NaOH to produce a
mixture of six compounds, not three, since the double bond formed can be in three different places and each
of the alkenes formed exists as a mixture of two optical isomers.

In the explanation that follows, the carbon atom bonded to bromine in compound A is called C
1 and the other
atoms in the cyclohexyl ring are numbered clockwise. If compound A forms a C=C bond between C1 and C6

Question 38

Hydrogen iodide is added to an evacuated reaction vessel. The vessel is sealed and warmed. A decomposition reaction occurs. Hydrogen and iodine are formed. Some hydrogen iodide remains.

When equilibrium is established, the total pressure is 1.20 × 10⁵ Pa. The partial pressure of hydrogen is 4.00 × 10³ Pa.

Hydrogen iodide, hydrogen and iodine are all gaseous under the conditions used.

What is the value of Kₚ for the equilibrium at this temperature, assuming the decomposition is the forward reaction?

Hydrogen iodide, hydrogen and iodine are all gaseous under the conditions used.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 14

The most common incorrect answer was C. Since the partial pressure of hydrogen at equilibrium is
4.00 x 10
3 Pa, and one molecule of iodine forms when one molecule of hydrogen forms, the partial pressure
of iodine at equilibrium is also 4.00 × 103 Pa. Since the total pressure at equilibrium is 1.20 × 105 Pa the
partial pressure of hydrogen iodide at equilibrium is 1.12 × 105 Pa (1.20 × 105 – (2 × 4.00 × 103)).
Using the equilibrium expression for the decomposition of hydrogen iodide gives a value for Kp of
1.28 × 10
–3.

subject: chemistry
stem:
The mass spectrum of compound X has M, M+1 and M+2 peaks. Other peaks are also present.

Peak M is the molecular ion peak, M⁺. Peak M has a relative abundance fifteen times that of peak M+1.

Peaks M and M+2 are of equal height.

What could be compound X?
stem_lead:
The mass spectrum of compound X has M, M+1 and M+2 peaks. Other peaks are also present.

Peak M is the molecular ion peak, M⁺. Peak M has a relative abundance fifteen times that of peak M+1.

Peaks M and M+2 are of equal height.

What could be compound X?

options.A: 1-chloro-2,2-dimethylpentane
options.B: 2-chloro-3-methylpentane
options.C: 2-bromo-2-methylhexane
options.D: 3-bromo-2,2-dimethylbutane

examiner_comment.text:
Question 40

The most common incorrect answer was C. Peaks M and M+2 are of equal height, so compound X is a
bromine compound. The correct answer must be C or D. To deduce the number of carbon atoms in a
compound the formula from 22.2.5 in the syllabus is required.100 ÷ (1.1 × 15) gives the answer 6.06, so
there are six carbon atoms per molecule. This confirms the correct answer as D and not C.

Cambridge International Advanced Subsidiary and Advanced Level
9701 Chemistry June 2023
Principal Examiner Report for Teachers

  © 2023
CHEMISTRY

learn_by_solve.solve: M and M+2 equal height → bromine (1:1), not chlorine (3:1). M is 15× (M+1) so n_C ≈ 100/(1.1×15) ≈ 6.06 → six carbons. 3-bromo-2,2-dimethylbutane. Examiner: C was the common error (bromo but seven carbons).

The infrared spectrum of compound Y is shown.

The reference table gives these characteristic infrared absorption ranges: C–O, hydroxy or ester, 1040–1300 cm⁻¹; C=C, aromatic compound or alkene, 1500–1680 cm⁻¹; C=O, amide 1640–1690 cm⁻¹, carbonyl or carboxyl 1670–1740 cm⁻¹, ester 1710–1750 cm⁻¹; C≡N, nitrile, 2200–2250 cm⁻¹; C–H, alkane, 2850–2950 cm⁻¹; N–H, amine or amide, 3300–3500 cm⁻¹; O–H, carboxyl 2500–3000 cm⁻¹, hydroxy 3200–3600 cm⁻¹.

What is the identity of compound X?
stem_lead:
Compound X reacts with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ to form compound Y.

The infrared spectrum of compound Y is shown.

The reference table gives these characteristic infrared absorption ranges: C–O, hydroxy or ester, 1040–1300 cm⁻¹; C=C, aromatic compound or alkene, 1500–1680 cm⁻¹; C=O, amide 1640–1690 cm⁻¹, carbonyl or carboxyl 1670–1740 cm⁻¹, ester 1710–1750 cm⁻¹; C≡N, nitrile, 2200–2250 cm⁻¹; C–H, alkane, 2850–2950 cm⁻¹; N–H, amine or amide, 3300–3500 cm⁻¹; O–H, carboxyl 2500–3000 cm⁻¹, hydroxy 3200–3600 cm⁻¹.

What is the identity of compound X?

options.A: propan-1-ol
options.B: propan-2-ol
options.C: propanone
options.D: propanoic acid

headers: characteristic infrared absorption range (in wavenumbers) / cm⁻¹

learn_by_solve.solve: X is oxidised by acidified dichromate to Y. Y’s IR is a carboxylic acid (canyon + C=O). Primary alcohol → acid under reflux with excess oxidant. X is propan-1-ol. Propan-2-ol would give a ketone; propanone does not oxidise; propanoic acid is already Y, not X.

B.pathway: Student conflates 2° oxidation (ketone) with 1° oxidation (acid).

followup.stem: Excess hot acidified dichromate: what is the organic product from propan-2-ol?

options.A: Propanoic acid
options.B: Propanone
options.C: Propanal
options.D: No reaction? it already is an acid

followup.why: Y is an acid, so X was the primary alcohol, not propan-2-ol.

C.pathway: Student omits that ketones are not oxidised by this reagent.

followup.stem: Does propanone react with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ to give a carboxylic acid?

options.A: Yes, all carbonyls oxidise to acids
options.B: No — ketones are not oxidised under these conditions
options.C: Yes, to propan-1-ol
options.D: Yes, to an alkene

followup.why: X cannot already be the ketone if Y is a new oxidation product that is an acid.

D.pathway: Student reverses X and Y: the acid is the product, not the starting alcohol.

followup.stem: The question asks for X, the reactant. Y is the oxidation product whose IR is shown. If Y is propanoic acid, what is X?

options.A: Propanoic acid
options.B: Propanone
options.C: Propan-1-ol (oxidised all the way to the acid)
options.D: An alkene

followup.why: D is Y, not X.

stem:
The mass spectrum of CH₃Cl shows a molecular ion peak, M⁺, at the m/e value of 50 with a relative abundance of 18.0%.

Other peaks are present in the mass spectrum.

What is seen in the mass spectrum at the m/e value of 52?
stem_lead:
The mass spectrum of CH₃Cl shows a molecular ion peak, M⁺, at the m/e value of 50 with a relative abundance of 18.0%.

Other peaks are present in the mass spectrum.

What is seen in the mass spectrum at the m/e value of 52?

options.A: a peak with relative abundance of 4.5%
options.B: a peak with relative abundance of 6.0%
options.C: a peak with relative abundance of 18.0%
options.D: a peak with relative abundance of 54.0%

learn_by_solve.solve: CH₃Cl: M at 50 is ¹²C¹H₃³⁵Cl. M+2 at 52 is ³⁷Cl. ³⁵Cl:³⁷Cl = 3:1, so abundance at 52 = 18.0% × 1/3 = 6.0%.

A.pathway: Student used 1/4 (perhaps ¹²C/¹³C logic) on the chlorine pair.

followup.stem: ³⁵Cl:³⁷Cl ≈ 3:1. If M (³⁵Cl) is 18.0%, M+2 (³⁷Cl) is?
followup.why: The chlorine isotope ratio is 3:1, not 4:1.

C.pathway: Student set M+2 equal to M, as if bromine.

followup.stem: Equal M and M+2 is the bromine pattern. Chlorine is 3:1. Should m/e 52 equal 18.0%?

options.A: Yes
options.B: No — it should be one-third of 18.0%
options.C: Yes, because ³⁷Cl is as common as ³⁵Cl
options.D: Yes, because of ¹³C

followup.why: Do not import the bromine 1:1 ratio.

D.pathway: Student reversed 3:1 and made M+2 three times M.

followup.stem: 3:1 means the lighter chlorine is more abundant. M+2 should be smaller or larger than 18%?

options.A: Larger (54%)
options.B: Smaller (6%)

Question 25
This question was concerned with safe replacements for the CFCs that destroy the ozone layer.  Only 13%

2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃; ΔH negative

examiner_comment.text:
Question 39  turned on the ability of concentrated sulphuric acid to carry out a dehydration.  52% of
candidates appreciated that this can be done wi th both secondary and tertiary alcohols (key B), but 25% of

tertiary alcohol, when tertiary alcohols dehydrate far more readily than secondary and primary alcohols.

In four questions there appears to have been an element of guessing, where candidates were uncertain of
the chemistry involved.

stem:
Samples of 10 cm³ of each of the first four members of the alkane series are separately mixed with 70 cm³ of oxygen. Each is then burned and the total volume, V, of residual gas measured again at room temperature and pressure.

Which graph represents the results that would be obtained?

Which graph represents the results that would be obtained?

options.A: Graph of V / cm³ against alkane: CH₄ = 10, C₂H₆ = 20, C₃H₈ = 30, C₄H₁₀ = 40.
options.B: Graph of V / cm³ against alkane: CH₄ = 30, C₂H₆ = 50, C₃H₈ = 70, C₄H₁₀ = 90.
options.C: Graph of V / cm³ against alkane: CH₄ = 50, C₂H₆ = 40, C₃H₈ = 30, C₄H₁₀ = 20.
options.D: Graph of V / cm³ against alkane: CH₄ = 60, C₂H₆ = 55, C₃H₈ = 50, C₄H₁₀ = 45.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 4 involved a graphical display of the quantitative re sults of burning the first four members of the
homologous series of alkanes in an excess of oxygen: there was an almost even distribution among the four
options.

Although Question 11  performed satisfactorily, only 36% of  candidates chose the correct answer B.
Examiners have noted in the past that  candidates have difficulty in deter mining the proportions of reactants
and products from a given value of K
c.

When potassium bromide is heated with  concentrated sulphuric acid ( Question 17 ), 41% of candidates
believed that only potassium hydrogensulphate and hydrogen bromide are produced (distractor A): only 22%
were aware of the oxidising properties of sulphuric ac id in knowing that bromine, water and sulphur dioxide
are also produced (key D).

The structure of a cyclic ester was given in Question 40.  67% of candidates thought this to be a ketone, and
37%, in not recognising it as an ester, did not identify the carbon-oxygen bond that is broken on hydrolysis.
9701 Chemistry November 2006
2
CHEMISTRY

examiner_comment.text:
Question 31  was another novel question which proved much too challenging.  If a 1 mol sample of a
monomer was completely polymerized by addition polym erization, how many moles of polymer might,
theoretically, be formed?  No less than 83% of candidat es thought that one possibl e answer was 1.  That
would mean that the polymer would have had the same number of molecules as did the starting material,
which must therefore be identical to the monomer.  The opposite extreme would be if all 6.02x1023 molecules
reacted to form a single chain polymer, and this would result in one molecule, but only 1/6.02x10 23 of a mole
– only 26% appreciated that this could be an answer.

Two other questions, while performing satisfactorily, deserve comment.

If N₂O₄ gas is placed in a sealed vessel the following equilibrium is established.

The forward reaction is endothermic.

2  The partial pressure of NO₂ increases.
3  The activation energy is unchanged.

3  The activation energy is unchanged.

options.B: 1 and 2 only are correct
options.C: 2 and 3 only are correct
options.D: 1 only is correct

statements.text: The partial pressure of NO₂ increases.

Therefore it can be deduced that this question rested for many on the truth or ot herwise of statement 3.
Statement 3 says “The activation energy is unchanged”. An increase in temperature will not change the
activation energy of the reaction, so statement 3 is true.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 39

15% of candidates chose the correct answer, B. The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was A,
chosen by 42% of candidates. These statistics show that the majority of candidates realised that, on heating
with excess concentrated sulfuric acid, structures 1 and 2 produce only one product with molecular formula
C
7H10. However most of the candidates who got this far then decided that structure 3 would also produce
only one product with molecular formula C 7H10, so they chose A. However the OH group on the ring in
structure 3 can dehydrate in two ways, either across the bond nearer to the side chain or across the bond
further away from the side chain. These two dehydrations give two different products, and the key is B.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 37

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C. This suggests that most candidates knew that the three
carbon atoms in propane all lie in the same plane. The six carbon atoms in 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene also all lie
in the same plane, since the bond angles at an sp2 hybridised carbon atom are very close to 120°, and the  π
bond prevents rotation. However, the six carbon atoms in cyclohexane do not lie in the same plane, they are
all sp3 hybridised with bond angles close to 109°.

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was B. Answer B, propane, is incorrect because the bond
angle at each carbon atom is close to 109°. Answer D, sulfur hexafluoride, is correct as the bond angles are
all 90°, thus there are three sets of F-S-F atoms that form a straight line.

learn_by_solve.solve: which structure are three atoms bonded together in a straight line? Required: D — sulfur hexafluoride, SF₆. A would need “poly(ethene), (–CH₂CH₂–)ₙ”, but the item needs “sulfur hexafluoride, SF₆”. B would need “propane, C₃H₈”, but the item needs “sulfur hexafluoride, SF₆”. C would need “silicon tetrachloride, SiCl₄”, but the item needs “sulfur hexafluoride, SF₆”.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 9

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was A. If b moles of HI are there at the start, the total number
of moles present will always be b. At equilibrium the partial pressure of HI is p(b–x)/b. The partial pressures
of H
2 and I2 are both px/2b. If these values are put into the equilibrium expression we get x2/4(b–x). The
choice of A suggests many candidates did not appreciate that each mole of HI gives half a mole of H2 and
half a mole of I2.

stem:
J is a branched-chain alcohol, C₅H₁₂O. J is heated under reflux with an excess of Cr₂O₇²⁻ / H⁺ until no further reaction occurs. An organic compound K is formed in good yield.

The infra-red spectrum of K is shown.

What are the structures of the branched-chain alcohol J and compound K?
stem_lead:

What are the structures of the branched-chain alcohol J and compound K?

options.A: J: CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₂OH; K: CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CHO
options.B: J: CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₂CH₃; K: CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH₃
options.C: J: CH₃CH(CH₃)CH(OH)CH₃; K: CH₃CH(CH₃)COCH₃
options.D: J: CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₂OH; K: CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂COOH

examiner_comment.text:
Question 30

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was D. From the infra-red spectrum, K clearly has a C=O
group but no COOH group; it is therefore an aldehyde or a ketone. This rules out D. The conditions stated in
the question would oxidise an aldehyde to a carboxylic acid. Therefore, K is a ketone and J must be a
secondary alcohol. The answer cannot be B as this structure does not have a branched chain. Therefore, the
answer is C.

learn_by_solve.solve: K’s IR is C=O without a carboxyl canyon, so aldehyde or ketone. Excess reflux dichromate would oxidise an aldehyde on to an acid, and the question says good yield of K — so K is a ketone and J a secondary alcohol. J is branched C₅H₁₂O. B is unbranched. C fits. Examiner: D was the common error (acid).

options.A: It is the final product
options.B: It is oxidised on to a carboxylic acid
options.C: It is reduced to a primary alcohol
options.D: It is unchanged

followup.why: K cannot be the aldehyde. Examiner used this to kill A.

B.pathway: Student picks a secondary alcohol → ketone pair but omits ‘branched-chain’.

followup.stem: J is stated to be a branched-chain alcohol. Is pentan-3-ol branched?

options.A: Yes, any secondary alcohol is branched
options.B: No — CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₂CH₃ is a straight chain
options.C: Yes, because it has five carbons
options.D: No, because ketones cannot be branched

followup.why: B is the right chemistry on the wrong skeleton.

D.pathway: Student conflates the acid product of a primary alcohol with the ketone actually on the IR.

followup.stem: K’s IR shows C=O but no COOH canyon. What is K?

options.A: Carboxylic acid
options.B: Ketone (or aldehyde, but aldehyde would not survive these conditions)
options.C: Alcohol
options.D: Alkene

followup.why: Examiner: D was the most common wrong answer; the canyon is missing.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 39

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C. This was a challenging question involving careful
thought.
• If compound 1 undergoes an addition reaction with steam, butane-1,3-diol is produced. If this is
oxidised, 3-oxobutanoic acid is produced. Statement 1 is therefore true.
• If compound 2 undergoes a substitution reaction with OH
–, 3-hydroxybutanoic acid is produced. If this is
oxidised, 3-oxobutanoic acid is produced. Statement 2 is therefore true.
• If compound 3 undergoes a substitution reaction with OH –, 3-hydroxybutanal is produced. If this is
oxidised, it gives 3-oxobutanoic acid. Statement 3 is therefore true.

All three statements are true, so therefore the answer is A.

9701 Chemistry November 2018

The infra-red spectrum of compound L is shown.

What could be the structure of L?
stem_lead:
The infra-red spectrum of compound L is shown.

What could be the structure of L?

options.A: HOCH₂COCH₂OH
options.B: HOCH₂CH(OH)CHO
options.C: HOCH₂CH(OH)CH₂OH
options.D: HOCH₂CH₂COOH

learn_by_solve.solve: Broad alcohol O–H, C–O, no C=O: glycerol HOCH₂CH(OH)CH₂OH. A and B have C=O (ketone/aldehyde); D has a carboxyl canyon.

A.pathway: Student sees C=O and also names a hydroxyketone/hydroxyaldehyde, omitting that an alcohol O–H would still have to be present.

followup.stem: A molecule with both a ketone C=O and an alcohol O–H must show which pair of bands?

options.A: Sharp C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹ only
options.B: Broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ only
options.C: Both a sharp C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹ and a broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹
options.D: A nitrile band at 2200–2250 cm⁻¹

followup.why: Both groups are independent absorbers. Missing the alcohol O–H rules out a hydroxyketone.

options.B: Broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ only
options.C: Both a sharp C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹ and a broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹
options.D: A nitrile band at 2200–2250 cm⁻¹

followup.why: Both groups are independent absorbers. Missing the alcohol O–H rules out a hydroxyketone.

followup.stem: Which extra feature, besides a C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹, is required before you can call the compound a carboxylic acid?

options.A: A sharp peak at 2200–2250 cm⁻¹
options.B: A very broad O–H absorption spanning about 2500–3000 cm⁻¹
options.C: A sharp peak at 3300–3500 cm⁻¹
options.D: No absorption above 1500 cm⁻¹

followup.why: Carboxyl O–H is a canyon from about 2500–3000 cm⁻¹. A ketone has C=O without that canyon.

J is a branched-chain alcohol, C₅H₁₂O. J is heated under reflux with an excess of Cr₂O₇²⁻/H⁺ until no further reaction occurs. An organic compound K is formed in good yield.

The infra-red spectrum of K is shown.

What are the structures of the branched-chain alcohol J and compound K?
stem_lead:

The infra-red spectrum of K is shown.

What are the structures of the branched-chain alcohol J and compound K?

options.A: J: CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₂OH; K: CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CHO
options.B: J: CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₂CH₃; K: CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH₃
options.C: J: CH₃CH(CH₃)CH(OH)CH₃; K: CH₃CH(CH₃)COCH₃
options.D: J: CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₂OH; K: CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂COOH

examiner_comment.text:
Question 30

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was D. From the infra-red spectrum, K clearly has a C=O
group but no COOH group; it is therefore an aldehyde or a ketone. This rules out D. The conditions stated in
the question would oxidise an aldehyde to a carboxylic acid. Therefore, K is a ketone and J must be a
secondary alcohol. The answer cannot be B as this structure does not have a branched chain. Therefore, the
answer is C.

learn_by_solve.solve: K’s IR is C=O without a carboxyl canyon, so aldehyde or ketone. Excess reflux dichromate would oxidise an aldehyde on to an acid, and the question says good yield of K — so K is a ketone and J a secondary alcohol. J is branched C₅H₁₂O. B is unbranched. C fits. Examiner: D was the common error (acid).

A.pathway: Student stops at aldehyde and omits that excess reflux dichromate oxidises aldehydes to acids.

followup.stem: Under the stated conditions (excess Cr₂O₇²⁻/H⁺, heat, until no further reaction), what happens to an aldehyde?

options.A: It is the final product
options.B: It is oxidised on to a carboxylic acid
options.C: It is reduced to a primary alcohol
options.D: It is unchanged

followup.why: K cannot be the aldehyde. Examiner used this to kill A.

B.pathway: Student picks a secondary alcohol → ketone pair but omits ‘branched-chain’.

followup.stem: J is stated to be a branched-chain alcohol. Is pentan-3-ol branched?

options.A: Yes, any secondary alcohol is branched
options.B: No — CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₂CH₃ is a straight chain
options.C: Yes, because it has five carbons
options.D: No, because ketones cannot be branched

followup.why: B is the right chemistry on the wrong skeleton.

D.pathway: Student conflates the acid product of a primary alcohol with the ketone actually on the IR.

followup.stem: K’s IR shows C=O but no COOH canyon. What is K?

options.A: Carboxylic acid
options.B: Ketone (or aldehyde, but aldehyde would not survive these conditions)
options.C: Alcohol
options.D: Alkene

followup.why: Examiner: D was the most common wrong answer; the canyon is missing.

options.D: 1 only is correct

examiner_comment.text:
Question 39

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C. This was a challenging question involving careful
thought.
• If compound 1 undergoes an addition reaction with steam, butane-1,3-diol is produced. If this is
oxidised, 3-oxobutanoic acid is produced. Statement 1 is therefore true.
• If compound 2 undergoes a substitution reaction with OH
–, 3-hydroxybutanoic acid is produced. If this is
oxidised, 3-oxobutanoic acid is produced. Statement 2 is therefore true.
• If compound 3 undergoes a substitution reaction with OH –, 3-hydroxybutanal is produced. If this is
oxidised, it gives 3-oxobutanoic acid. Statement 3 is therefore true.

All three statements are true, so therefore the answer is A.

Cambridge International Advanced Subsidiary and Advanced Level
9701 Chemistry November 2018
Principal Examiner Report for Teachers

  © 2018
CHEMISTRY

The infra-red spectrum of compound P is shown.

What could be compound P?

learn_by_solve.solve: Broad alcohol O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹, no C=O, isopropyl CH₃ ~1375 cm⁻¹ and 2° C–O ~1130 cm⁻¹: propan-2-ol. Ester and aldehyde need C=O; acid needs the carboxyl canyon.

options.C: A sharp peak at 3300–3500 cm⁻¹
options.D: No absorption above 1500 cm⁻¹

examiner_comment.text:
Question 40

Option C was a common incorrect choice. To select the correct option, each compound had to be looked at
separately.
• Compound 1 produces CH
3COOH, CH2OHCH2COOH and CH3OH.
• Compound 2 produces CH 3OH and HOOCCH(CH3)CH2COOH.
• Compound 3 produces CH 2OHCH(CH2OH)CH2CH2COOH and CH3COOH.

Compound 1 is therefore the only compound to produce three different organic products when hydrolysed.
Hence, option D is the correct response.

The products from each compound are those formed by hydrolysis with water or hot HCl (aq). If hot
NaOH(aq) is used, the sodium salts of the acids would be obtained, but the same number of products would
be formed in each case.

stem:
Substance T was analysed and found to contain 62.07% carbon, 10.34% hydrogen and 27.59% oxygen.

The infra-red spectrum of substance T is shown.

Which substance could be T?
stem_lead:
Substance T was analysed and found to contain 62.07% carbon, 10.34% hydrogen and 27.59% oxygen.

The infra-red spectrum of substance T is shown.

Which substance could be T?

options.A: cyclohexane-1,4-diol; SMILES: OC1CCC(O)CC1
options.B: 3-methylpentanoic acid; SMILES: CCC(C)CC(=O)O
options.C: propanone; SMILES: CC(=O)C
options.D: pentane-1,5-diol; SMILES: OCCCCCO

learn_by_solve.solve: C 62.07%, H 10.34%, O 27.59% → C₆H₁₂O₂. IR is alcohol O–H, no C=O: a diol. Cyclohexane-1,4-diol is C₆H₁₂O₂. Pentane-1,5-diol is C₅H₁₂O₂. The acid has C=O+canyon; propanone is C₃H₆O with C=O.

B.pathway: Student matches composition loosely and omits that the IR has no carboxyl C=O/canyon.

followup.stem: 3-methylpentanoic acid has C=O and carboxyl O–H. If the IR is an alcohol without C=O, is the acid possible?

options.A: Yes
options.B: No
options.C: Yes, if the percentages match
options.D: Yes, acids never show C=O

followup.why: IR already kills the acid.

C.pathway: Student recognises a ketone IR in memory and ignores both composition and the O–H on the plot.

followup.stem: Propanone is C₃H₆O. Does 62% C / 27% O match C₃H₆O?

options.A: Yes
options.B: No — propanone is far too small and would show C=O, not alcohol O–H
options.C: Yes if you ignore hydrogen
options.D: Yes, all ketones are C₆H₁₂O₂

followup.why: Wrong formula and wrong functional group.

D.pathway: Student gets ‘diol, no C=O’ and then fails the empirical-formula arithmetic (C₅ vs C₆).

followup.stem: Pentane-1,5-diol is C₅H₁₂O₂ (O = 32/104 ≈ 30.8%). The data are O = 27.59%. Which diol matches C₆H₁₂O₂ (O = 32/116 ≈ 27.6%)?

options.A: Pentane-1,5-diol
options.B: Cyclohexane-1,4-diol
options.C: Propanone
options.D: Any C₅ acid

followup.why: Right functional group, wrong carbon count.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 40

Option C was a common incorrect choice. To select the correct option, each compound had to be looked at
separately.
• Compound 1 produces CH
3COOH, CH2OHCH2COOH and CH3OH.
• Compound 2 produces CH 3OH and HOOCCH(CH3)CH2COOH.
• Compound 3 produces CH 2OHCH(CH2OH)CH2CH2COOH and CH3COOH.

Compound 1 is therefore the only compound to produce three different organic products when hydrolysed.
Hence, option D is the correct response.

The products from each compound are those formed by hydrolysis with water or hot HCl
 (aq). If hot
NaOH(aq) is used, the sodium salts of the acids would be obtained, but the same number of products would
be formed in each case.

stem:
Which statements are correct?

1  enthalpy of combustion of H₂ = enthalpy of formation of H₂O 2  enthalpy of formation of H₂ = −(enthalpy of atomisation of H₂) 3  enthalpy of solution of HCl = enthalpy of hydration of H⁺ + enthalpy of hydration of Cl⁻
stem_lead:
Which statements are correct?

1  enthalpy of combustion of H₂ = enthalpy of formation of H₂O 2  enthalpy of formation of H₂ = −(enthalpy of atomisation of H₂) 3  enthalpy of solution of HCl = enthalpy of hydration of H⁺ + enthalpy of hydration of Cl⁻

options.A: 1, 2 and 3 are correct
options.B: 1 and 2 only are correct
options.C: 2 and 3 only are correct
options.D: 1 only is correct

statements.text: enthalpy of combustion of H₂ = enthalpy of formation of H₂O
enthalpy of formation of H₂ = −(enthalpy of atomisation of H₂)
enthalpy of solution of HCl = enthalpy of hydration of H⁺ + enthalpy of hydration of Cl⁻

examiner_comment.text:
Question 32

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was A. The correct answer is D.

• Statement 1 is correct. The complete combustion of one mole of hydrogen produces one mole of water.
• Statement 2 is incorrect. the enthalpy of formation of any element is defined as zero, while the enthalpy
of atomisation of any element that consists of diatomic molecules requires the absorption of a finite and
measurable amount of energy to break bonds.
• The enthalpy of solution of HCl requires the breaking of the H–Cl bond as well as the hydration of the two
ions mentioned, so statement 3 is also incorrect.

stem:
The structure of compound R is shown.

Which statements about compound R are correct?

1  It has an Mᵣ of 116.
2  It contains two groups that show strong absorptions between 1640 and 1740 cm⁻¹ in its infrared spectrum.
3  Its only infrared absorption between 2500 and 3000 cm⁻¹ is sharp and strong.

2  It contains two groups that show strong absorptions between 1640 and 1740 cm⁻¹ in its infrared spectrum.
3  Its only infrared absorption between 2500 and 3000 cm⁻¹ is sharp and strong.

options.A: 1, 2 and 3 are correct
options.B: 1 and 2 only are correct
options.C: 2 and 3 only are correct
options.D: 1 only is correct

statements.text: It contains two groups that show strong absorptions between 1640 and 1740 cm⁻¹ in its infrared spectrum.
Its only infrared absorption between 2500 and 3000 cm⁻¹ is sharp and strong.

learn_by_solve.solve: From the structure, Mᵣ = 116 (statement 1). Two carbonyl groups → two strong 1640–1740 cm⁻¹ bands (statement 2). 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ is not ‘only a sharp C–H’: a carboxyl O–H canyon is there, so 3 is false. Key B.

A.pathway: Student treats the carboxyl O–H canyon as a sharp C–H and admits statement 3.

followup.stem: A sharp strong band near 2900 cm⁻¹ is C–H. A very broad 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ absorption is which bond?

options.A: C–H as well
options.B: Carboxyl O–H
options.C: C≡N
options.D: C=C

followup.why: Statement 3 is false, so not ‘all three’.

C.pathway: Student drops the Mᵣ count (operation on the structure).

followup.stem: Mᵣ is the sum of the atomic masses on the displayed structure. If that sum is 116, is statement 1 true?

options.A: No, Mᵣ cannot be read from a structure
options.B: Yes
options.C: Only if the IR agrees
options.D: Only for hydrocarbons

followup.why: 1 and 2 are both true.

D.pathway: Student omits the two carbonyls in 1640–1740 cm⁻¹.

followup.stem: Two separate C=O groups each absorb in 1640–1740 cm⁻¹. Does that make statement 2 true?

options.A: No, only one C=O ever appears
options.B: Yes
options.C: No, C=O is at 3200 cm⁻¹
options.D: Only for ketones, never acids/esters

followup.why: Do not drop statement 2.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 20

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C.
The double bonds at positions 1 and 7 each have a CH2 group. This will not give rise to geometric isomers, so
these two bonds need not be considered. The double bonds at positions 3 and 5 both give rise to geometric

Question 32

Each of the answers was chosen by approximately equal numbers of candidates.
• Statement 1 is correct. The complete combustion of one mole of hydrogen produces one mole of water.
• Statement 2 is incorrect. The enthalpy of formation of any element is defined as zero, while the enthalpy
of atomisation of any element that consists of diatomic molecules requires the absorption of a finite and
measurable amount of energy to break bonds.
• Statement 3 is also incorrect. The enthalpy of solution of HC l requires the breaking of the H –Cl bond as
well as the hydration of the two ions mentioned.

3  Its only infrared absorption between 2500 and 3000 cm⁻¹ is sharp and strong.

learn_by_solve.solve: From the structure, Mᵣ = 116 (statement 1). Two carbonyl groups → two strong 1640–1740 cm⁻¹ bands (statement 2). 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ is not ‘only a sharp C–H’: a carboxyl O–H canyon is there, so 3 is false. Key B.

A.pathway: Student treats the carboxyl O–H canyon as a sharp C–H and admits statement 3.

followup.stem: A sharp strong band near 2900 cm⁻¹ is C–H. A very broad 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ absorption is which bond?

options.A: C–H as well
options.B: Carboxyl O–H
options.C: C≡N
options.D: C=C

followup.why: Statement 3 is false, so not ‘all three’.

C.pathway: Student drops the Mᵣ count (operation on the structure).

followup.stem: Mᵣ is the sum of the atomic masses on the displayed structure. If that sum is 116, is statement 1 true?

options.A: No, Mᵣ cannot be read from a structure
options.B: Yes
options.C: Only if the IR agrees
options.D: Only for hydrocarbons

followup.why: 1 and 2 are both true.

D.pathway: Student omits the two carbonyls in 1640–1740 cm⁻¹.

followup.stem: Two separate C=O groups each absorb in 1640–1740 cm⁻¹. Does that make statement 2 true?

options.A: No, only one C=O ever appears
options.B: Yes
options.C: No, C=O is at 3200 cm⁻¹
options.D: Only for ketones, never acids/esters

followup.why: Do not drop statement 2.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 37

The most common incorrect answer was C. Each statement will be treated separately.

Statement 1 is true.
Statement 2 is true. When the upper C=C bond is oxidised both limonene and terpinolene give a product with
a ketone group and an acid group in the same positions on the carbon skeleton. However, when the lower
C=C bond is oxidised the ketone group forms on a different carbon atom.
Statement 3 is untrue. Limonene forms a compound with four chiral carbon atoms, as the carbon atom at the
4 position of the six-membered ring becomes chiral. Terpinolene forms a compound with three chiral carbon
atoms.

options.D: No absorption above 1500 cm⁻¹

examiner_comment.text:
Question 21

The most common incorrect answer was C.
In this explanation it will be considered that HBr adds on to the central C=C bond first.

Cambridge International Advanced Subsidiary and Advanced Level
9701 Chemistry November 2021
Principal Examiner Report for Teachers

  © 2021
Since the molecule is symmetrical it does not matter how the first HBr adds to the central C=C bond. When
the second HBr adds on, the bromine atom can go on either the 2 or the 3 position of the left hand ring.
When the third HBr adds on, the bromine atom can go on either the 2 or the 3 position of the right hand ring.
The four compounds that form can therefore be called ‘2,2’, ‘2,3’, ‘3,2’ and ‘3,3’. Since the addition of the first
HBr made the molecule asymmetrical ‘2,3’ and ‘3,2’ are different, giving four different products.

2  An excess of hot concentrated acidified KMnO₄ reacts with limonene and with terpinolene to form different diketo acids.

2  An excess of hot concentrated acidified KMnO₄ reacts with limonene and with terpinolene to form different diketo acids.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 37

The most common incorrect answer was A. Each statement will be treated separately.

Statement 1 is true.
Statement 2 is true. When the upper C=C bond is oxidised both limonene and terpinolene give a product with
a ketone group and an acid group in the same positions on the carbon skeleton. However, when the lower
C=C bond is oxidised the ketone group forms on a different carbon atom.
Statement 3 is untrue. Limonene forms a compound with four chiral carbon atoms, as the carbon atom at the
4 position of the six-membered ring becomes chiral. Terpinolene forms a compound with three chiral carbon
atoms.
